beats.say: Hi! Some sites open a small window to sign you in. Today you will learn to spot a fake one.
A scammer draws that window inside the page, like a picture. Even its address bar looks right.

body.text: Sign in with your work email to view the document.

beats.say: The test is simple: grab the window and drag it outside the browser. A fake one cannot leave the page.
If your password manager does not fill in the password, stop. Type the address in a new tab yourself.

scenes.prompt: Which sign-in window can you trust?

body.text: It reached the edge of the page and was cut off.

cards.explain: A real window leaves the browser and goes anywhere on the screen. If it gets cut off, it is a picture drawn inside the page.

body.text: You dragged the window aside: it left the browser and moved onto the desktop.
ParolSeyf offered the password by itself.

cards.explain: The window moves apart from the browser, and the password manager recognises the site. These are signs of a real window.

body.text: No saved password found for this site.
Address written in the window: poct.idare.example

cards.explain: A password manager checks the real address of the site, not the text in the window. If it finds no password, the site is a different one.

body.text: You dragged the browser itself aside.
The sign-in window moved along with it.

cards.explain: A real window stays where it is. If it moves together with the browser, it is part of the page.

body.text: The password manager filled in the password.

cards.explain: When you type the address yourself, a fake window has no way in. This is the most reliable way.

scenes.title: Tender document
scenes.intro: A supplier sent a link to a tender document. The site wants you to sign in to show it. Go carefully.

steps.label: Tender document: office furniture purchase
steps.say: The document is locked. The site offers sign-in with your work account.

actions.label: Sign in with IshPocht
actions.feedback: Pressing the button is not dangerous yet. The real test is the window that opens now.

actions.label: Check the address
actions.feedback: This is the tender site, not your work mail. Watch the sign-in window that opens next very closely.

actions.label: Close the tab
actions.feedback: A careful choice. Open your mail yourself, and ask the supplier for the document another way.

body.text: Sign in with your work email to view the document.

steps.say: The window shows the right address. But that proves nothing yet.

actions.label: Drag the window outside the browser
actions.feedback: The right test. Let us see whether the window can leave the browser.

actions.label: Fill with ParolSeyf
actions.feedback: Good idea. The password manager checks the real address of the site.

actions.label: Type the password and sign in
actions.feedback: The address bar in the window was only a picture. Your password went to the owner of the tender site.

actions.label: Cancel
actions.feedback: Good. Never type a password into a window you are not sure about.

body.text: The window reached the edge of the page and was cut off.
It did not leave the browser.

steps.say: The window was cut off at the page edge. A real window never does that.

actions.label: Close the window and the tab
actions.feedback: Right. A window that cannot leave the page is fake, so type nothing into it.

actions.label: Sign in anyway
actions.feedback: You had already seen that the window was fake. Your password went to the scammer.

actions.label: Report the site to technical support
actions.feedback: Excellent. Technical support can block the site and protect your colleagues too.

steps.say: The password manager found no password for this site.

actions.label: Type the password manually
actions.feedback: The password manager was right: this site is not your mail. The password you typed went to the scammer.

actions.label: Stop and close the window
actions.feedback: Right. When the password manager does not fill in, stopping is the best move.

steps.say: You typed the address in a new tab. The password manager filled in the password.

actions.label: Sign in
actions.feedback: Right. When you type the address yourself, a fake window has no way in.

actions.label: Check the address
actions.feedback: This is your real work mail, and the password manager recognised it. Signing in is safe.

steps.label: Document not found
steps.say: The password is gone and the document never opened. Act fast now.

actions.label: Change the password and call technical support
actions.feedback: Right. Change the password in a new tab, and let technical support close all open sessions.

actions.label: Sign in again
actions.feedback: The site collects your password a second time. It is a trap for passwords, not a document.

actions.label: Do nothing
actions.feedback: The scammer can already open your mail with that password. Change it and report it right away.

scenes.prompt: Put the steps in order when a sign-in window looks suspicious.

items.label: Drag the window outside the browser
If it cannot leave, close the window and the tab
Type the address in a new tab and sign in there
Report the site to technical support

scenes.explain: First test, then close, then type the address yourself. Report the site so your colleagues are protected too.

points: Drag a sign-in window outside the browser: a fake one cannot leave
If the password manager does not fill in, stop
When in doubt, type the address in a new tab yourself
